description: This IEEE Transactions on Power Delivery paper by Horton, Boteler, Overbye, Pirjola and Dugan (October 2012) publishes a small synthetic high-voltage transmission network with substations, transformers, line resistances and grounding data, together with reference results, so that software for computing geomagnetically induced currents (GIC) can be checked against a common benchmark. It is a fictitious test system, not tied to a real utility, and gives geographic coordinates so that a uniform geoelectric field can be applied. The data are tables inside the article, obtained through IEEE Xplore, which is paid or institutional access under IEEE copyright; Crossref metadata read on 2026-09-28 confirm the bibliographic details, but the IEEE page itself renders only by script. Caveats: the network is small and synthetic, it uses a uniform electric field assumption, and it is reproduced in many later tools, not maintained. It is used for hazard exposure and resilience analysis of power grids to space weather, and for validating GIC network flow models. Related records: data-powermodelsgmdlib-gic-test-cases and model-power-network-model-gic implement GIC test cases, and data-great-britain-grid-gic-open-data is a real-network counterpart.
